tabs.label: Where it shows
tabs.description: One bar, two pages, two switches. The cart ships off so that page is untouched until you say otherwise.

fields.label: Show it on the checkout
fields.help: The bar under the Payment section, at the foot of the checkout.

fields.label: Show it on the cart page
fields.help: Off, so the cart page is exactly as it is today until you turn this on. It is the same bar with the same words — there is no second set to keep in step.

tabs.label: On a phone
tabs.description: The same bar at 900px and below, with its own shape. Ruled rows is what ships here and spread-to-both-edges is what ships on a desktop, which is the pair the owner chose; the switch at the top hands the phone back to the desktop's settings.

fields.label: Give the phone its own shape
fields.help: On, because a bar that reads as one line on a desktop reads as a scramble at 390px. Everything below is read only while this is on; with it off the phone gets the desktop's settings exactly as it always did.

fields.label: Shape on a phone
fields.help: At 900px and below.

options.bar: One line — everything on a single row
options.split: Two columns — brand on one side, contact on the other
options.stack: Stacked — brand, then help, then the links
options.rows: Ruled rows — each block on its own line, with a hairline between

fields.label: Alignment on a phone
fields.help: At 900px and below.

fields.label: Space above the bar on a phone
fields.help: Its own value, because a gap that reads right under a 1240px page is usually too much under a 390px one.

fields.label: Height on a phone
fields.help: Padding above and below together, at 900px and below. The two under it override it one at a time.

fields.label: Padding inside the top, on a phone
fields.help: Between the top edge of the bar and its first row. This is the one to reach for when the bar sits too close to the Place order box above it.

fields.label: Padding inside the bottom, on a phone
fields.help: And under the last row.

fields.label: Padding inside each row on a phone
fields.help: Ruled rows is the shipped phone shape, so this is the control that decides how tall the bar is there. 7 is what it worked out from the phone block gap before.

fields.label: Smallest row height on a phone
fields.help: A floor under each ruled row. 44 is the touch-target minimum if you want every row tappable.

fields.label: Side padding on a phone
fields.help: Between the screen edge and the first word. 20 lines the bar up with the checkout's own page padding.

fields.label: Space between blocks on a phone
fields.help: Between the brand, the help line, the contacts and the links.

fields.label: Text size on a phone
fields.help: A multiplier on 12px, at 900px and below.

fields.label: Brand size on a phone
fields.help: The wordmark alone, at 900px and below. Follows the desktop brand size until you move it.

tabs.label: Shape & size
tabs.description: Four structures and four alignments, which is sixteen looks from two controls. "One line" left-aligned is the shortest, and is what ships.

fields.label: Shape
fields.help: The structure. All four carry the same words; what changes is how they are grouped. Pair it with Alignment below.

options.bar: One line — everything on a single row
options.split: Two columns — brand on one side, contact on the other
options.stack: Stacked — brand, then help, then the links
options.rows: Ruled rows — each block on its own line, with a hairline between

fields.label: Alignment
fields.help: Where the content sits across the bar. "Spread to both edges" pushes the first block hard left and the last hard right, with the gap taken up in the middle — the classic footer look, and the one that reads worst when there are only two blocks left.

fields.label: Background
fields.help: Tones from the shop's own palette rather than a colour box: a footer that can be set to anything is a footer that can be set to something unreadable.

options.pink: Blush — the shop's own soft pink

fields.label: Line above the bar
fields.help: A hairline between the page and the footer. Off on the dark tone usually reads better, because the colour already separates them.

fields.label: Line thickness
fields.help: Only while the line above is on.

fields.label: Rounded top corners
fields.help: Rounds the two top corners, which lifts the bar off the page rather than sitting it flush. Works best with a tone that is not the page's own.

fields.label: Lift it off the page
fields.help: A soft shadow above the bar. It reads as a separate surface rather than as the end of the page — worth it with a rounded or contrasting tone, and usually not otherwise.

fields.label: Space above the bar
fields.help: Between the last block on the page and the top of the bar. The page's own background shows through it, so it reads as a gap rather than as more footer.

fields.label: Height
fields.help: Padding above and below together. The two controls under it override this one at a time; leave them alone and the bar is symmetric, as it was.

fields.label: Padding inside the top
fields.help: Between the top edge of the bar and its first line. Left where it is, it follows "Height" above.

fields.label: Padding inside the bottom
fields.help: And under the last line. Left where it is, it follows "Height" above.

fields.label: Padding inside each row
fields.help: Above and below each row of the "Ruled rows" shape, and the space the hairline sits in. 9 is what the shape worked out from the block gap before this had a number of its own.

fields.label: Smallest row height
fields.help: A floor under each ruled row, whatever the padding says. Zero is the row taking exactly the height of its words; 44 is a comfortable tap target on a phone.

fields.label: Side padding
fields.help: Between the screen edge and the first word.

fields.label: Content width
fields.help: Where the words stop. The bar itself always runs the full width of the window.

options.page: Line it up with the page above it
options.fixed: A width of my own, set below

fields.label: That width
fields.help: Read only while "A width of my own" is chosen above.

fields.label: Where the policy links sit
fields.help: Only the one-line shapes have a choice here; the stacked and ruled-row shapes put every block on its own line anyway.

options.brand: Under the wordmark, with the byline
options.inline: At the end of the row

fields.label: Space between blocks
fields.help: Between the brand, the help line, the contacts and the links. On a phone they wrap, and this is the gap on both axes.

fields.label: Text size
fields.help: Everything in the bar except the brand, which has its own size below. A multiplier on 12px.

fields.label: The wordmark
fields.help: The header's own logo, colours and weight — read live from Appearance → Header, so the two cannot drift apart.

fields.label: Brand size
fields.help: The wordmark alone. A multiplier on 14px.

fields.label: Brand in capitals
fields.help: On is the wordmark as it reads today. Off leaves whatever capitalisation is typed into the brand field.

fields.label: The mark beside the phone
fields.help: The glyph is WhatsApp's either way. This is whether it is drawn in the bar's own ink or in WhatsApp green.

options.mono: The bar's own colour — what it does today

fields.label: Separator between blocks
fields.help: A mark in the space between the brand, the help line, the contacts and the links. Drawn only on the one-line shapes, where blocks sit side by side and a separator has somewhere to go.

fields.label: Marks beside the phone and email
fields.help: The small WhatsApp and envelope glyphs. Off leaves the number and the address as plain text, which is shorter and quieter.

fields.label: Back-to-top arrow
fields.help: A small arrow at the far end of the bar. It scrolls the page rather than jumping, and it is hidden from screen readers only if it has no label.

fields.label: Arrow style
fields.help: How the arrow is drawn.

tabs.label: Content
tabs.description: Every word in the bar. Anything left empty is not drawn at all, rather than drawn empty — so the bar can be as short as a brand and a phone number.

fields.label: Brand name
fields.help: Drawn only while "The wordmark" above is set to the typed name. Leave it empty to draw no brand at all.

fields.label: Under the brand
fields.help: The company line. Empty draws nothing.

fields.label: Help heading
fields.help: Empty draws nothing.

fields.label: Help line
fields.help: Empty draws nothing.

fields.label: Phone shown
fields.help: Exactly as it should read. Empty removes the phone and its mark.

fields.label: Phone link
fields.help: Where tapping the number goes — a wa.me link for WhatsApp, or tel: to dial. Only http, https, tel and mailto links are accepted; anything else is drawn as plain text rather than as a link.

fields.label: Email shown
fields.help: Empty removes the email and its mark. It is linked with mailto: automatically.

fields.label: First link
fields.help: Empty removes the link.

fields.label: First link goes to
fields.help: A path on this shop, or a full https:// address.

fields.label: Second link
fields.help: Empty removes the link.

fields.label: Second link goes to
fields.help: A path on this shop, or a full https:// address.

fields.label: Third link
fields.help: Empty, so no third link is drawn. Returns and refunds is the usual one.

fields.label: Third link goes to
fields.help: A path on this shop, or a full https:// address.

fields.label: Small print
fields.help: A last line under the rest — a copyright, a licence number, a registered address. Empty draws nothing at all.

fields.label: Arrow label
fields.help: Read out by a screen reader; never shown. Empty hides the arrow from screen readers entirely, which is right only if the page has another way back up.

tabs.label: Payment marks
tabs.description: Off by default. The drawings themselves are a hardcoded constant — these switches only decide which of the six is printed.

fields.label: Show the payment marks
fields.help: A row of scheme marks in the bar. Off by default — it is a claim about what this shop accepts, so it is worth turning on deliberately and switching off the ones that are not true.

fields.label: Visa
fields.help: Only drawn while the row above is on.

fields.label: Mastercard
fields.help: Only drawn while the row above is on.

fields.help: Only drawn while the row above is on.

fields.help: Only drawn while the row above is on.

fields.help: Only drawn while the row above is on.

fields.label: Tamara
fields.help: Only drawn while the row above is on.

tabs.label: Layout
tabs.description: Which cart page this shop serves, and whether it carries the site footer.

fields.label: Cart page layout
fields.help: Classic is the page as it is today. Squeezed is the docked-bar layout: dense product rows, a full-width recommended rail, the minimal coupon box and the two sticky rows at the foot of the screen.

options.classic: Classic — the page as it is today

fields.label: Show the site footer on the cart page
fields.help: Off, as asked: the cart page ships with no footer at all. THE CART PAGE ONLY — the footer still appears on the homepage, on product pages, on /shop/ and on every other page of the shop, and this switch cannot affect them. Turn it on to bring the footer back to the cart page; it applies to both the classic and the squeezed cart layouts.

tabs.label: Product rows · the squeezed layout
tabs.description: ONLY on the Squeezed layout — these four are custom properties that the classic cart page does not read. One height drives the whole line; everything in it is worked out from that number.

fields.label: Row height
fields.help: The single control for how dense the basket is. The thumbnail, the type sizes and the quantity stepper are all worked out from it, so they shrink with the row instead of overflowing it.

fields.label: Text size in rows
fields.help: A nudge multiplied INTO the size the row height already produced, never an override — so this slider and the one above can never fight, and neither can silently win.

fields.label: Bold text in rows
fields.help: On is what the rows do today. Off gives every line regular weight.

fields.label: Size of the − / + quantity stepper
fields.help: The minus, the plus and the number between them. A multiplier and not a fixed size: the stepper is worked out from the row height like everything else in the line, so it still shrinks when you shorten the row — this nudges that result up or down. The digit scales with the box, so it stays centred at every setting.

tabs.label: Product rows · spacing and size
tabs.description: An ORDINARY product’s row on the cart page, on whichever layout this shop serves, and never a set’s row — a set has its own controls under Appearance → Set. Laptop values; the phone has its own card below. Nothing here can hide what is in the row: the height control is a minimum, so it can only make a row taller.

fields.name: ci_min_h
fields.label: Minimum row height
fields.help: A FLOOR AND NEVER A CEILING. Zero — what the page draws today — lets every row be exactly as tall as what is in it. Raise it and a short row grows; a tall one is never cut, which is the one thing this control must not be able to do.

fields.name: ci_pad_s
fields.label: Row padding, leading edge
fields.help: The left-hand side in English and the RIGHT-hand side on /ar — it is a logical property, so it mirrors with the page instead of staying on one side of it.

fields.name: ci_gap
fields.label: Space between the picture and the words

fields.name: ci_thumb
fields.label: Picture size
fields.help: The square at the start of the row. The floor is 28px: below that it stops being a picture anybody can read at arm’s length.

fields.name: ci_brand_on
fields.label: Show the brand name
fields.help: The small uppercase brand line above each product name, on a laptop or desktop. The phone has its own switch on the next card.

fields.name: ci_brand_f
fields.label: Brand size
fields.help: The small uppercase line above the product name. A row whose product has no brand has never drawn one.

fields.name: ci_name_f
fields.label: Name size
fields.help: IN TENTHS OF A PIXEL, because the phone’s shipped size is 12.5px and a slider stores whole numbers: 130 is 13px. The floor is 100 — 10px — which is a size, not a way of hiding the name.

fields.name: ci_name_gap
fields.label: Space under the name
fields.help: What separates the name from whatever is under it — the option line or the quantity stepper.

tabs.label: Product rows · phone
tabs.description: The phone’s own values for the same row, and the width it starts at. They never inherit the laptop’s — the shipped stylesheet already differs at both widths, so an inheriting field would have to ship already touched to reproduce today’s page.

fields.name: ci_bp
fields.label: The product rows switch to their phone sizes below
fields.help: ▲ 600, which is the width resources/css/kbb/kbb-cart.css already turns this page over at. Moving it away from 600 leaves a band of widths where the sheet’s own numbers and these disagree, because a media query is resolved before custom properties exist and the compiled sheet cannot be told a new number.

fields.name: ci_gap_m
fields.label: Space between the picture and the words

fields.name: ci_brand_on_m
fields.label: Show the brand name
fields.help: Off, as asked: a phone shows the product name without the brand line above it. Turn it on to bring the brand back on phones.

fields.name: ci_name_f_m
fields.label: Name size
fields.help: In tenths of a pixel: 125 is 12.5px, which is half a pixel smaller than the laptop’s and is what the sheet’s own phone block draws.

tabs.label: Recommended
tabs.description: Full width, no rounded corners, no padding box around it.

fields.label: Show the recommended rail
fields.help: Renders nothing at all until products are chosen below, so this can stay on in a shop that has not picked any.

fields.label: Products across the screen
fields.help: In tenths: 45 is four and a half cards. The half card is the point — a card cut off by the screen edge is what tells a thumb there is more to the right. Card width is a fraction of the screen, so the count holds on every phone.

fields.label: Bold product names in the rail
fields.help: Off, as asked. The price below the name has its own switch — until you move that one it follows this.

fields.label: Bold prices in the rail
fields.help: Follows the product-name switch above until you move it. From then on it is its own setting and the two are independent.

fields.label: Line height of product names
fields.help: How far apart the two lines of a product name sit. The name is clamped to two lines and the box is worked out from this, so a looser setting gives the second line room rather than cutting it off.

fields.label: Space under the product name
fields.help: The gap between the name and the price under it.

fields.label: Space under the picture
fields.help: The gap between the product picture and the name under it.

fields.label: Size of the + button
fields.help: A multiplier on the one-tap add button, not a pixel size: the button is worked out from the screen width like the rest of the card, so it stays in proportion on every phone and this nudges that result.

fields.label: Move the + left or right
fields.help: Zero leaves it on the corner of the picture. Positive pushes it further out past that corner, negative tucks it back inside. It is measured from the corner it sits on, so it mirrors in a right-to-left shop.

fields.label: Move the + up or down
fields.help: Zero leaves it on the corner of the picture. Positive lifts it, negative drops it.

fields.label: Background movement
fields.help: The rail sits on a slow wash of colour. 0 holds it still. It is directly above the checkout button, so it is deliberately quiet — and it stops entirely for anyone whose phone asks for reduced motion.

tabs.label: Summary & trust
tabs.description: The figures under the coupon box, and the row of marks below them.

fields.label: Express Delivery Charge row
fields.help: Off, because this shop does not offer express delivery yet. THE EXPRESS FIGURE IS NEVER ADDED TO THE TOTAL even when this is on: the reference shows it priced beside a free Standard and a total that matches Standard, so it is an option a shopper picks at checkout, not a charge applied behind them.

fields.label: Express delivery charge
fields.help: Quoted, not added. See the switch above.

fields.label: Express (i) note
fields.default: Delivered the next working day where available. Chosen at checkout.
fields.value: Delivered the next working day where available. Chosen at checkout.

fields.label: Standard Delivery row
fields.help: Off, so the cart page does not try to answer a question the checkout answers properly. While it is off, the shop's own free-delivery bar takes its place in the summary — the green congratulations once an order qualifies, and how much more would qualify it before that.

fields.label: Standard (i) note
fields.default: Free on every order. Two to four working days.
fields.value: Free on every order. Two to four working days.

fields.label: Line shown when there is no free-delivery threshold
Service Fee row
fields.help: Off, and while it is off no fee is charged either — the row and the money are one switch, not two.

fields.label: Service fee · percentage
fields.help: Worked out on the order value AFTER any coupon, so a discount reduces the fee with it.

fields.label: Size of the trust row
fields.help: The tick, the wording and the payment marks together — they are one line, so one number moves all of it.

tabs.label: Docked rows
tabs.description: The two rows that stay at the foot of the screen.

fields.label: Delivery address row
fields.help: Drawn only while Appearance → Checkout page → Fields & attention → "Address picker row on cart and checkout" is on. That switch ships off, so this one decides nothing until it is turned on.

fields.label: Text in both rows
fields.help: Everything in both docked rows is a multiple of this, so no wording can outgrow the bar it sits in.

fields.label: Space under the checkout row
fields.help: Extra white space below the docked rows. Zero is where they sit today, on the bottom edge. On a phone with a home indicator this is added to the space the hardware already reserves, not used instead of it.

fields.label: Text in the delivery row
fields.help: The delivery row only — its wording, the address under it and the button on the right. Multiplied into the size "Text in both rows" already produced, so this and that slider stack rather than overrule one another, and the checkout row below is left where it is.

fields.label: Weight of the delivery row text
fields.help: The heading — "Please choose your delivery address", and "Delivering to Home" once one is picked. Medium is what the row is today. The address line under it stays regular; the button has its own setting below.

fields.label: Address button text size
fields.help: The "+ Address" / "Change address" button only. Multiplied into the size "Text in both rows" already produced, so the two sliders stack rather than overrule one another.

fields.label: Weight of the address button
fields.help: The "+ Address" / "Change address" button only. Semi-bold is what it is today.

fields.label: Checkout button wording
fields.help: It shares the docked row with the item count and the total, so a longer word here is a narrower tally beside it. The button gives way first and ends in an ellipsis rather than pushing the figures off a 360px screen.

fields.label: Address row · once chosen
fields.help: Use {tag} where Home or Office should appear.

tabs.label: Desktop
tabs.description: The two-column cart page, from 1024px up. Everything here is read only on desktop — none of it can reach a phone.

fields.label: Two-column layout on desktop
fields.help: From the width below, the basket and the Recommended rail take the left column and everything else moves to the right. Off, a desktop gets the phone layout stretched across the screen, which is what it did before this existed.

fields.label: Desktop starts at
fields.help: Screens narrower than this keep the phone layout exactly as it is. 1024 leaves an iPad in portrait (768px) on the phone layout, which is the right call: two columns need room.

fields.label: Widest the page will go
fields.help: The two columns stop growing here and centre themselves. A basket row stretched across a 27-inch monitor is unreadable.

fields.label: Products across the rail
fields.help: In tenths: 55 is five and a half cards. The half card is deliberate — it is what tells someone the rail carries on past the edge. Desktop only; the phone keeps its own count under Recommended.

fields.label: Carousel arrows on the rail
fields.help: A round button at each end of the Recommended rail. Desktop only; a phone swipes instead, and the half card already tells it there is more.

fields.label: Quantity buttons on desktop
fields.help: Multiplied into the size "Product rows" already produced, so the phone keeps its own number and this adjusts it for desktop.

fields.label: Page side padding
fields.help: Space between the edge of the page and the columns.

fields.label: Space between sections
fields.help: Between the basket and the Recommended rail on the left, and between the summary and the checkout block on the right.

fields.label: Padding inside a section
fields.help: Inside the basket card, the rail and the summary — the space between a section's border and what it holds.

fields.label: Padding inside the checkout box
fields.help: The box holding the delivery address and Proceed to Checkout. It has its own number because it is the only section that is mostly a button.

fields.label: Right column follows the scroll
fields.help: The summary and Proceed to Checkout stay on screen while a long basket scrolls past. Off, they sit at the top and scroll away with the page.

fields.label: Gap above it when it sticks
Address popup width
fields.help: On a phone the address popup rises from the bottom edge. On desktop there is no bottom edge worth rising from, so it is a panel centred over the page.

tabs.label: Address popup
tabs.description: Its two heights — one for the list, a taller one for the form — its density and every word in it.

fields.label: New-address popup height · upright
fields.help: The popup that holds the FORM — the one with the fields in it. It grows from the bottom to fit what is in it and stops here. THE POPUP ITSELF NEVER SCROLLS — if a long address list would not fit, the list scrolls inside its own box and the Home / Office / Deliver here row stays put at the bottom where a thumb can reach it.

fields.label: Address-list popup height · upright
fields.help: The popup that holds the SAVED LIST — the one that opens first for a signed-in shopper who already has an address. Shorter than the form above it, because choosing needs less room than typing. Past this the list scrolls inside its own box; the popup itself still never does, so + Add New Address stays where a thumb can reach it.

fields.label: New-address popup height · on its side
fields.help: Used when the phone is held horizontally. The fields go two across and the address list goes two across at the same time.

fields.label: Address-list popup height · on its side

tabs.label: What is recorded
tabs.description: Three switches. Turning one off stops new rows of that kind; it never deletes what is already there.

fields.label: Record administrative changes
fields.help: Settings, back-office accounts and core-update packages: who changed what, from which address, and what it said before. Off, nothing is written and the screen below stays empty from that moment on — the rows already recorded are kept.

fields.label: Record sign-ins and failed sign-ins
fields.help: Every admin sign-in and sign-out, every wrong password, and every time the login throttle turned somebody away. The password itself is never recorded, only the email that was tried.

fields.label: Record rate-limit trips
fields.help: When the shop answers 429 — too many requests — it says so to that visitor and forgets. This remembers it. It does not change who is refused; nothing here refuses anything.

fields.label: Collapse repeat trips within
fields.help: Repeat trips from the same address on the same path land on one row with a count, for this many seconds, instead of one row each. A flood is then one row that says 4,000 rather than 4,000 rows.

tabs.label: The verdict line
tabs.description: The one sentence at the top of this screen, and the two numbers that decide whether it says "nothing to do" or "look at this".

fields.label: The verdict covers the last
fields.help: The line at the top of the screen counts what happened in this many hours. The lists below it are not limited to it.

fields.label: Failed sign-ins before it says look
fields.help: Below this the verdict reads "nothing above the usual". At or above it, it says so plainly and names the addresses.

fields.label: Rate-limit trips before it says look
fields.help: The same, for requests the shop answered 429. A shop with a busy crawler trips this honestly, which is why it is a number you can move rather than a fixed one.

tabs.label: File integrity
tabs.description: Whether the shop checks that the files its packages installed are still the files those packages contained — and what it does when one is not. It reports; it changes nothing on disk.

fields.label: Check that shipped files still match their package
fields.help: Every update package carries a SHA-256 for each file it installs. This hashes those files on the server and reports any that differ, or that are gone. It can only speak about files a package installed — not uploads, not anything hand-created, and not a file somebody ADDED, which has no hash to miss.

fields.label: Check again at most every
fields.help: Opening this screen runs the check when the last one is older than this. It is a file-by-file hash on this host, so it is throttled rather than run on every refresh; "Check now" on the card ignores this.

fields.label: When a file does not match
fields.help: Today there is one answer and it is the recommended one: tell you, and change nothing. Restoring the file from the package that installed it is genuinely possible — the package is still on this server — but it is a WRITE, and it would also silently undo a legitimate hand-edit. That decision is yours to take, and the second option appears here when you have taken it.

tabs.label: Content security policy
tabs.description: Whether the shop tells browsers what it is allowed to load, and collects what falls outside that. It reports; it refuses nothing, and there is no setting on this screen that can make it refuse.

fields.label: Send the report-only content-security policy
fields.help: Tells every visitor's browser what this shop is allowed to load — and asks it to REPORT anything outside that rather than block it. Nothing is refused, no page changes, and no shopper sees anything different. While it is on, browsers post a short report for each thing the policy would have stopped, and those land in the list above. Turn it on for a week when you want to know what switching enforcement on would cost; the list fills up in minutes.

fields.label: What the policy does
fields.help: There is one answer today and it is the one the plan calls for: report, and refuse nothing. Enforcing comes after the request gate has watched real traffic, and it comes one rule at a time — a policy switched to enforce in one step is how a working checkout stops taking cards. The second option appears here when that round arrives.

options.report: Report only — collect violations, refuse nothing

fields.label: Collapse repeat violations within
fields.help: The same violation on the same page lands on one row with a count, for this many seconds, instead of one row per visitor. Without it a single inline script would write one row for every page view on the shop.

fields.label: Never keep more than
fields.help: The ceiling on violation rows, separately from the one on everything else. It matters because this is the only thing in this table a stranger can cause: without a ceiling of its own, enough posted violations would push your sign-ins and setting changes out of the trail to make room. Violations can never take more than this many rows.

tabs.label: Evidence & retention
tabs.description: How much of the trail this screen draws, how long any of it is kept, and the ceiling that holds when nobody opens this screen.

fields.label: Rows shown in each list
fields.help: How many of the newest rows each of the three lists draws. It does not affect what is recorded or what the verdict counts.

fields.label: Keep evidence for
fields.help: Rows older than this are deleted when this screen is opened. Evidence is personal data — an address and an email — and it should expire on a schedule rather than accumulate for ever. There is no scheduler on this host, so "when this screen is opened" is the whole of it; the ceiling below is what holds on a shop nobody opens it on.

fields.label: Never keep more than
fields.help: The hard ceiling on the whole trail. When it is passed, the oldest rows go until the count is back under it — and that happens as rows are written, not when this screen is opened, so it holds on a shop nobody ever visits this screen on. It is the backstop for "keep evidence for" above, not a replacement for it.

fields.label: Store addresses with the last part masked
fields.help: Records 203.0.113.x instead of the whole address. It costs you the ability to tell two visitors on one network apart, which is usually the thing you wanted the address for — so it ships off, and is here for a shop that would rather not hold the last part at all.

classic.note: The badge this store ships with — gold stars, the heart, the count and the sold note.

minimal.label: Minimal
minimal.note: Stars and the score, nothing else. The quietest option on a busy product page.

trust.label: Trust green
trust.note: Leads with the number of shoppers rather than with the score.

blush.label: Blush
blush.note: K-beauty pink. The same information as Classic, a softer colour.

mono.label: Mono
mono.note: Grey stars, no heart, no sold note — for a monochrome theme.

fields.label: How this store sends email
fields.help: Leave this on "Use this server's mail" unless your host has told you otherwise — it needs nothing filled in below. Pick the SMTP option only if you have a mailbox on a dedicated mail server, and then fill in the six boxes under it. The last option sends nothing at all and is for checking a template.
options: Send nothing — write to the log (for testing only)

fields.label: SMTP host
fields.help: From the hosting control panel, e.g. smtp.hostinger.com

fields.label: Port
fields.help: 465 with SSL, or 587 with TLS. Shared hosts commonly block 25.

fields.label: Encryption
fields.help: ssl for port 465, tls for port 587, none only on a local relay.

fields.label: Username
fields.help: Usually the full mailbox address, e.g. no-reply@kbeautybliss.com

fields.label: Password
fields.help: The mailbox password. Stored encrypted and never shown again once saved.

fields.label: From address
fields.help: What customers see as the sender. On most shared hosts this MUST be a mailbox on this domain or the host rejects the message.

fields.label: From name
fields.help: e.g. K Beauty Bliss

fields.label: New-order alerts to
fields.help: Where you want to be told an order has come in. Leave blank to use the From address above.

fields.label: Timeout (seconds)
fields.help: How long to wait for the mail server before giving up. Blank uses the default. Only used by the dedicated-SMTP option.

fields.label: Support WhatsApp number
fields.help: Printed in every order confirmation as a "Chat on WhatsApp" link. Blank uses the number the storefront footer already shows.

fields.label: Support email address
fields.help: Where a customer should write for help. Ships as info@kbeautybliss.com, which the owner asked for. Clear it and the Reply-To or From address is used instead.

fields.label: Instagram
fields.help: Your handle (@kbeauty.bliss) or the full profile link. Blank uses the one saved under Store → Business Details.

fields.label: Signature
fields.help: Signed at the foot of every order email, e.g. "With love, the K Beauty Bliss team". Type a | where you want a new line. Blank prints the store name.

fields.label: Cancelled orders: what you tell a paid customer about their money
fields.help: Added to the cancellation email ONLY when the order was paid and no refund has been recorded against it yet — e.g. how you send the money back and how long it takes. Leave blank and the email says nothing beyond the amount and that no refund has been recorded.

fields.label: Dispatch email: how long delivery takes AFTER DISPATCH
fields.help: Printed after "Your order has left us and is with the courier." on orders going to the UAE. Measured from the moment the parcel leaves you — not from when the order was placed, which is what the delivery line under Place order (Store → Delivery & Shipping) measures, so the two are separate boxes on purpose. Leave blank and the email keeps its current wording. Orders outside the UAE are given no window at all, because none has been measured.

fields.label: Reply-To address
fields.help: Where a customer's reply to an order email goes. Set this and every order email invites the customer to reply and says the reply reaches you. Leave it blank and no such invitation is printed, because with the From box empty this store sends as no-reply@ and a reply would reach nobody.

fields.label: Google account address
fields.help: The Google Workspace mailbox that signs in to send, e.g. info@kbeautybliss.com. The From address must be this account or one of its aliases (Gmail → Settings → Accounts → "Send mail as"); Google rewrites any other From to this address.

fields.label: Google app password
fields.help: A 16-letter app password, not your normal Google password: Google Account → Security → 2-Step Verification → App passwords. Spaces are ignored. Stored encrypted and never shown again once saved.

fields.label: Dubai address
fields.help: Printed at the foot of every order email. Type a | where you want a new line. Leave blank to use the store address saved under Store → Business Details.

fields.label: Korea address
fields.help: Printed at the foot of every order email under the Dubai address. Type a | where you want a new line. Leave blank and no Korea address is printed.
